Masinissa of Numidia seizes the Emporia from Carthage

timeline: Deep desert of the eastern Sahara, crossed by few

states.name: Murzuq

states.name: Butnan

states.name: Ajdabiya
timeline: Augila oasis, where the Nasamones gather dates each summer

states.name: Ash Shati
timeline: Wadi ash-Shati, northern valley of the Garamantes

states.name: Ghat

Cato the Younger marches his army along the Syrtis to Leptis
Both sides of the Altars of the Philaeni now answer to Rome

states.name: Misrata
timeline: Coast east of Leptis, the Punic sphere's edge on the Gulf of Sirte
Masinissa of Numidia seizes the Emporia from Carthage

states.name: Murqub
timeline: Leptis, chief city of the Emporia, pays tribute to Carthage
Masinissa raids the Emporia; Carthage appeals to Rome in vain
Masinissa of Numidia seizes the Emporia from Carthage
Leptis seeks Rome's friendship and receives a Roman garrison, while Numidian kings still claim it
Caesar fines Leptis three million pounds of olive oil a year for backing Juba

states.name: Tripoli District

Masinissa of Numidia seizes the Emporia from Carthage
After Thapsus, Caesar joins the Emporia to Rome's African provinces

states.name: Zawiya
timeline: Sabratha, a Punic trading post of the Emporia
Masinissa of Numidia seizes the Emporia from Carthage
After Thapsus, Caesar joins the Emporia to Rome's African provinces
Balbus's column sets out for the desert from the Tripolitanian coast

states.name: Al Qubbah

Ptolemy Apion bequeaths Cyrenaica to Rome

states.name: Jabal al Akhdar
timeline: Cyrene, the richest Greek city of Africa, on the Green Mountain
Ptolemy I of Egypt takes Cyrenaica
Magas rules Cyrene as an independent king
Cyrenaica rejoins Egypt through Berenice's marriage to Ptolemy III
Ptolemy Apion bequeaths Cyrenaica to Rome
Cyrenaica becomes a Roman province
Mark Antony gives Cyrenaica to Cleopatra Selene, daughter of Cleopatra
After Actium, Cyrenaica returns to Roman rule

states.name: Marj
timeline: Barca, Greek city of the plateau
Ptolemy I of Egypt takes Cyrenaica
Ptolemy Apion bequeaths Cyrenaica to Rome
Mark Antony gives Cyrenaica to Cleopatra Selene, daughter of Cleopatra
After Actium, Cyrenaica returns to Roman rule

states.name: Benghazi
timeline: Euesperides, westernmost Greek city of Cyrenaica
Ptolemy I of Egypt takes Cyrenaica
Refounded nearby as Berenice, for the Cyrenean queen of Egypt
Ptolemy Apion bequeaths Cyrenaica to Rome
Mark Antony gives Cyrenaica to Cleopatra Selene, daughter of Cleopatra
After Actium, Cyrenaica returns to Roman rule

states.name: Jafara

After Thapsus, Caesar joins the Emporia to Rome's African provinces

states.name: Mizdah
timeline: Libyan farmers and herders of the Gebel, behind the Emporia

states.name: Jufra
timeline: Oases of Waddan and Zella on the desert road between the Syrtis and the Fezzan

states.name: Sabha
timeline: Oases of the Garamantes around Sabha

states.name: Wadi al Hayaa
timeline: Garama grows in the Wadi al-Ajal, heartland of the Garamantes
Underground foggara channels water fields of wheat, barley and date palms
Balbus captures Garama; Rome claims a victory, but the kingdom endures

events.title: Altars of the Philaeni
events.text: Tradition places the border between Carthage and Cyrene at the altars of two Carthaginian brothers, buried alive to win the line.

events.title: Garama in the valley
events.text: By the 4th century BC, Garama is growing in the Wadi al-Ajal below the older hilltop village of Zinkekra.

events.title: Chariots on the rock
events.text: Painted two-wheeled chariots with galloping horses appear in the rock shelters of the Tadrart Acacus.

events.title: Herodotus's troglodytes
events.text: Herodotus, writing a generation earlier, says the Garamantes hunt 'cave-dwelling Ethiopians' from four-horse chariots.

events.title: Libyan revolt
events.text: After Carthage's disaster at Syracuse, its Libyan subjects and slaves rise and besiege the city.

events.title: Punic gold
events.text: Carthage begins to strike gold coins; where its gold came from is still debated.

events.title: Oracle of Ammon
events.text: Alexander the Great crosses the desert to the oracle at Siwa; Cyrene sends envoys to submit.

events.title: Ptolemy takes Cyrene
events.text: Ptolemy I's general Ophellas brings Cyrene and its cities under Egyptian rule.

events.title: Carthaginian stones
events.text: Theophrastus describes precious red 'carbuncles' brought from Carthage, later linked to the Garamantes.

events.title: Agathocles lands
events.text: The tyrant of Syracuse burns his ships on the African shore and marches on Carthage.

events.title: Ophellas's march
events.text: Ophellas leads an army through the Syrtic desert for two months to join Agathocles, who murders him.

events.title: King Magas
events.text: Magas, Ptolemy's stepson, rules Cyrene as an independent king for nearly thirty years.

events.title: Regulus lands
events.text: A Roman army lands at Clupea, carrying the First Punic War into Africa.

events.title: Elephants at Tunes
events.text: Carthage's North African war elephants crush Regulus's legions near Tunes.

events.title: Theveste taken
events.text: Hanno the Great conquers Theveste, pushing Carthage's lands deep into the interior.

events.title: Berenice
events.text: Berenice of Cyrene marries Ptolemy III; Euesperides is refounded in her name.

events.title: Mercenary War
events.text: Unpaid mercenaries and Libyan subjects revolt against Carthage after its defeat by Rome.

events.title: Scipio lands
events.text: Scipio lands near Utica, bringing the Second Punic War to Africa.

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.text: Scipio and the Numidian prince Masinissa defeat Hannibal; Carthage loses its empire.

events.title: Foggaras
events.text: The Garamantes dig underground channels to bring groundwater to their fields; the earliest dates are disputed.

events.title: Raids on the Emporia
events.text: Masinissa raids the Emporia, whose towns paid Carthage a talent of silver a day.

events.title: Masinissa's Emporia
events.text: With Rome's tacit approval, Masinissa seizes the Emporia from Carthage.

events.title: Third Punic War
events.text: Rome declares war on Carthage, accusing it of breaking the peace by fighting Masinissa.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: After a three-year siege, Rome razes Carthage and creates the province of Africa.

events.title: Leptis turns to Rome
events.text: During the Jugurthine War, Leptis asks the consul Metellus for a garrison and friendship.

events.title: Capsa falls
events.text: Marius crosses the desert to storm Jugurtha's stronghold of Capsa.

events.title: Apion's bequest
events.text: Ptolemy Apion dies and leaves Cyrenaica to the Roman people.

events.title: Province of Cyrene
events.text: Rome organises Cyrenaica as a province to collect its taxes.

events.title: Bagradas river
events.text: King Juba I of Numidia destroys Caesar's legate Curio and his army.

events.title: Cato's march
events.text: In winter, Cato the Younger leads Pompeian troops on foot along the Syrtis, with Psylli snake-charmers to treat the bitten.

events.title: Battle of Thapsus
events.text: Caesar defeats the Pompeians and Juba; Juba takes his own life and Numidia becomes Africa Nova.

events.title: Juba's camels
events.text: Among the spoils Caesar captures twenty-two of Juba's camels, an animal still rare in the Maghreb.

events.title: Oil for Caesar
events.text: Caesar fines Leptis three million pounds of olive oil a year.

events.title: Cleopatra Selene
events.text: In the Donations of Alexandria, Antony names his daughter by Cleopatra queen of Cyrenaica.

events.title: Imports reach Garama
events.text: Mediterranean amphorae and fine pottery begin to reach Garama in growing quantities.

events.title: Carthage rises again
events.text: Augustus settles Roman colonists on the site of Carthage, planned by Caesar.

events.title: Augustus's provinces
events.text: Africa Proconsularis and Crete-and-Cyrene become provinces governed by the Senate.

events.title: Cydamus taken
events.text: The proconsul Balbus marches inland from Sabratha and takes the oasis of Cydamus.

events.title: Garama taken
events.text: Balbus's column reaches Garama, the Garamantes' capital, the deepest Roman thrust into the Sahara yet.

events.title: Balbus's triumph
events.text: On 27 March in Rome, Balbus triumphs over the Garamantes, the last private citizen ever granted a triumph.

chartNote: Share of the area of present-day Libya, by the power that held or claimed each of today's districts. Ancient frontiers were not lines: control thinned away from the coast and the oases, and nomadic peoples crossed every district. The vast desert districts swing the shares; the map is a simplification.
